Liverpool have received encouraging news regarding Víctor Munoz after the winger suffered a worrying knee injury against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

The Spanish winger was forced off following a heavy collision during the first half of the 3-0 win, with the initial images raising fears of a potentially serious problem.

However, early tests have reportedly suggested that the injury is not as bad as first feared, offering Reds boss Andoni Iraola some welcome relief ahead of the Merseyside Derby on Sunday afternoon.

Munoz suffered the injury after his knee became caught during a strong collision with a Brugge player inside the opposition penalty area.

The incident prompted immediate concern among his teammates, with a stretcher brought onto the pitch to assist the winger. However, he eventually managed to leave the field under his own steam, accompanied by Dominik Szoboszlai.

It initially appeared particularly concerning, but subsequent tests have provided a more positive indication of the extent of the damage.

Recent findings suggest that according to reports from Spain, the initial assessment suggests that Munoz has suffered a 'severe' blow to his knee rather than a serious injury. Definitive confirmation is still pending, but the early indications are encouraging.

Iraola also offered a cautiously optimistic assessment after the match.

Industry observers note that "He felt a lot of pain at the moment, but by the end of the match he was feeling better. I hope it's nothing key," the Liverpool coach noted.

Although it remains unclear whether Munoz will be fit for this weekend's Merseyside derby, the initial diagnosis is certainly reassuring for Iraola.

The severity of the collision and the sight of the stretcher initially suggested that Liverpool could be facing a significant injury setback, potentially ruling the winger out for an extended period.

Instead, the early tests indicate that the problem may be limited to a heavy blow, although the club will understandably wait for definitive confirmation before making any decisions on his availability.

With a major fixture approaching, Muñoz's potential involvement would be a welcome boost, but avoiding a serious injury is the most notable outcome at this stage.

Chelsea are facing a potential problem surrounding Alejandro Garnacho.

The Argentine, firmly out of favour at Stamford Bridge, joined Aston Villa in the summer on a loan deal which included a conditional obligation to make the move permanent for £42.5million at the end of the season.

While the conditions that would trigger Garnacho’s permanent exit remain undisclosed, they are believed to involve the player making a certain number of appearances which Chelsea sources described at the time as easily achievable. Villa are also paying a loan fee.

However, with Garnacho being left out of four of Villa’s last five matchday squads, there is now growing doubt over whether the 22-year-old’s Chelsea exit will become permanent.

Chelsea placed a public valuation of £43m on Garnacho in July once the club’s hierarchy decided they wanted to sell him.

Garnacho’s initial preference had been to move overseas, and there was interest from Saudi Arabia, Serie A and elsewhere in Europe, until Villa made their interest known, shortly after selling their best player, Morgan Rogers, to Chelsea for £117m.

Garnacho has featured in just seven of Villa’s 19 games across all competitions so far this season, and is yet to start for Unai Emery’s side.

Garnacho’s exile continued this week in the Champions League clash at Galatasaray, where Emery decided to name just 11 out of a possible 12 substitutes - two of which were goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s latest absence, Emery said: “The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.”.

The Athletic have since reported that Villa are exploring their options to get rid of the player in January, though it remains to be seen if Chelsea would welcome such talks.

Chelsea and Villa could jointly agree to terminate the loan agreement, which would allow Garnacho to explore options elsewhere. But that would require both clubs agreeing to do so, and the chances of Chelsea getting a fee similar to the £42.5m Villa had committed to again appear slim.

The situation is threatening to become a headache which Chelsea believed they had remedied.

Chelsea may instead point to the chance that Garnacho’s minutes improve in the second half of the campaign as reason to keep the Argentine in situ.

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:31.

Tottenham Hotspur have suffered another injury setback, with Savio expected to miss several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem against Ipswich Town.

The Brazilian winger had only recently returned from a previous muscle injury before being forced off during last weekend's 2-0 victory in the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi now faces the prospect of being without the winger for a significant period during a busy end to 2026.

Savio made his first appearance since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United on October 10th when he came off the bench against the Tractor Boys.

However, his return lasted only around 20 minutes, with the 22-year-old going down inside the opposition penalty area after an impressive run before being helped from the pitch by Tottenham's medical staff.

His exact recovery timeline has not yet been determined, but The Athletic report that he is now expected to miss several weeks. One source has even said Savio could miss all seven of Tottenham's remaining matches in 2026.

De Zerbi confirmed that the winger had suffered a recurrence of the same muscle injury, expressing his frustration at losing an important member of his squad.

It has been revealed that "I'm very angry about that, because Savio is a crucial player for us," the Spurs boss remarked. "It's the same injury, and it is the worst thing from today.".

Savio has endured a difficult start to life in north London following his summer move from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £85m. Despite scoring on his debut against Charlton Athletic, he has managed just seven appearances due to fitness problems.

Tottenham already have significant attacking concerns, with Savio joining Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert on the injury list.

The north London outfit were already expected to explore the market for a new striker, but De Zerbi may now need to consider a more versatile forward capable of operating centrally and out wide.

That would help address the lack of options on the left flank, although Savio's absence could also create opportunities for academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old gem scored and assisted on his first Premier League start against Ipswich, offering De Zerbi an encouraging alternative.

However, with several attacking players unavailable and Savio potentially missing the remainder of the year, adding another forward in January would make sense.

Spurs need greater depth across their frontline, and a versatile signing could help address more than one problem at once.

Former Man United midfielder Darron Gibson has revealed the harrowing extent of his sleeping pill addiction and broke down in tears as his wife recalled the moment she thought he had died.

Gibson, who played for United 31 times between 2005-2012, secretly battled against anxiety during his career and turned to sleeping pills to help switch his mind off.

He began taking the pills after suffering a knee injury for the Republic of Ireland in 2013 and developed an addiction that led to him consuming 14 every night and on one occasion led to wife Danielle thinking he'd died.

Industry observers note that opening up on RTE’s Howler podcast, Danielle remembered her husband suffering a seizure in 2021, saying: 'When the ambulance staff came in, he had blue lips, I thought he had gone. I was being treated for shock. I just thought: "At least he’s not struggling anymore." Next minute (sharp intake of breath), he's back.'.

Gibson replied: 'Ultimately, if that hadn’t have happened, I wouldn’t be here now.'.

Danielle then said: 'I think you’d be dead', prompting Gibson to break down in tears, admitting 'probably'.

Darron Gibson (left) spoke about suffering from sleeping pill addiction and his wife Danielle (right) opened up about thinking he'd died in 2021 after a seizure.

Gibson broke down in tears at the painful memory but is now far happier and in recovery.

Gibson was convicted of drink driving in 2015 during his downward spiral and was playing for Everton at the time.

He added: 'Looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn’t go to sleep? It’s ridiculous. But it’s where I was. It’s what I was doing.

'I think Everton thought they were looking after me by not punishing me, which I really appreciated at the time.

Industry observers note that 'And I don’t blame them for any of this, but I think if they’d punished me, maybe I would have changed. But I didn’t and kept going.'.

Three years later at Sunderland, he consumed a mix of pills and vodka before crashing into parked cars. He was spared prison time but had a 40-month driving ban and the Black Cats ripped up his contract.

He recalled: 'Took a few sleeping tablets, thought I was going to go to sleep. Next thing I know, I’m in handcuffs in the back of a police van.'.

Danielle, who worked as a specialist in addiction services while Gibson was at Sunderland, states Gibson was one of many with similar issues in the professional game.

Sources indicate that she went on: 'I understand that football is a business. I just think they should have had a duty of care.

Gibson and Danielle are seen together at the Premier of Wayne Rooney's documentary in 2022.

Gibson poses with the Premier League trophy after Man United won the title in 2011.

'He’s not the only one that was struggling, there were so many lads, whether it be sleeping tablets or mental health or depression or anxiety or booze.

'There were so many that were almost denied access to services that I feel should have been available to all of them.'.

Gibson is now in recovery and states he is in a far happier state of mind than in his playing days. He ended his career at Salford City five years ago following a brief spell at Wigan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller tech giant she worked for.

Alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing manufacturer. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

Industry observers note that according to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the manufacturer advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

It has been revealed that this type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

It has been revealed that at the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the organization's website as of November 2026.

Industry observers note that "There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it said. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the Latest York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

It has been revealed that megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Sources indicate that alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the manufacturer's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

According to recent reports, in December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the organization was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell tech giant with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

Verdict: Total away goals over 2.5.

Hamburg have generally enjoyed a positive campaign despite recent setbacks.

The Green-Whites have collected three more points after 10 Bundesliga matches than they managed at the same stage last season, evidence that progress is being made under Daniel Thioune.

It has been revealed that however, results have taken a turn for the worse in recent weeks. Hamburg were heavily beaten 4-0 by Werder Bremen last weekend, and another defeat on Saturday could leave them just two points above the relegation zone.

According to recent reports, thioune’s side have now lost four of their last five matches in all competitions, scoring only five times while conceding 12 goals during that run. Those defensive struggles will be a major concern ahead of the visit of one of the division’s most dangerous attacking teams.

Sources indicate that history also offers little encouragement. Hamburg have not beaten Bayern since July 2011, a sequence that has included 17 defeats and three draws.

Despite that record, home form has been respectable. HSV have won three of their five Bundesliga matches at the Volksparkstadion this season, although they have also suffered two defeats there.

Sources indicate that hamburg have been dealt a significant blow with midfielder Nicolai Remberg ruled out for the remainder of the season. His absence could see Nicolas Capaldo continue in central midfield.

In attack, Yussuf Poulsen is unavailable, meaning Patson Daka is expected to lead the line. He could be supported by Fabio Vieira, who is likely to feature in an advanced role.

Bayern arrive under unusual pressure after suffering their first defeat of the season.

It has been revealed that the Bavarians were beaten 2-1 by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, a result that followed a disappointing 1-1 Bundesliga draw against FC Koln. Those results have raised concerns that Bayern could lose further ground in the title race if they fail to respond swiftly.

The defeat in France was also Vincent Kompany’s second match back on the touchline following his collapse in October, and the Belgian coach is still attempting to guide his side through a difficult spell.

Industry observers note that despite their recent frustrations, Bayern remain one of the Bundesliga’s strongest sides statistically. They have scored 30 goals in just 10 league matches, while only Borussia Dortmund have conceded fewer than their tally of 10.

According to recent reports, the champions’ loss to Lille was their first defeat in any competition this season and also their first away defeat. Before that setback, Bayern had won six and drawn three of their first nine away matches.

Off-field concerns have also generated headlines, with criticism directed at the club hierarchy over their handling of Jamal Musiala’s health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to publicly support his teammate.

Star striker Harry Kane is expected to miss several months with an ankle injury, while Michael Olise is a doubt for the trip to Hamburg.

There is better news regarding Luis Diaz, who should be available in some capacity, although Bayern may still be forced to deploy natural midfielder Konrad Laimer as their central attacking option.

Aleksandar Pavlovic was used in a more advanced role against Lille because of Bayern’s attacking injury crisis, but he is expected to return to midfield alongside Joshua Kimmich this weekend.

In a recent development, hamburg may feel they are catching Bayern at a favourable moment given the visitors’ injury list and recent drop in form. The absence of Harry Kane in particular removes a huge source of goals, while Kompany’s side are still recovering from their first defeat of the campaign.

Even so, Bayern possess significantly greater quality throughout the squad and remain one of the Bundesliga’s most potent attacking outfits. Hamburg’s defensive record in recent weeks is another concern, particularly against opposition capable of creating chances in volume.

The hosts should put up a fight, but Bayern are expected to respond positively to a difficult week and leave Hamburg with all three points.

Verdict: Total away goals over 2.5.

Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is key to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

According to recent reports, unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

Industry observers note that "I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

Industry observers note that although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

According to recent reports, the match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

It has been revealed that at some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

For now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

It has been revealed that “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”.

Sources indicate that kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”.

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Industry observers note that kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and remarked: “You held it together. You got through it.” It highlighted how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

According to recent reports, what a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

In a recent development, kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

In a recent development, kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg.

According to recent reports, for his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

According to recent reports, kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

According to recent reports, those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

According to recent reports, kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

According to recent reports, that work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and mentioned he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more notable than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

It has been revealed that kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

In a recent development, there's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN.

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”.

Recent findings suggest that the plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before promptly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

According to recent reports, the choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Industry observers note that kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

Recent findings suggest that in total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

Barcelona will continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are top of the La Liga table on 36 points, three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid, while Deportivo are 12th in the division.

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 06:47 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:49 EST, 26 November 2026.

The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident.

BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short.

But the midfielder, 23, refused to answer the interferer and instead told him: 'Sorry, she's got one more [question].'.

Bellingham, who scored a sensational long-range goal on the hour mark to put Real Madrid ahead in the Champions League clash, was widely praised after footage of the incident went viral on social media, with fans applauding him as a 'class act' and 'role model for young men'.

Now Conway has added to the praise, stating the experience 'added a whole latest layer to the love people have for Jude'.

Conway had been waiting to speak to the England star in the 'mixed zone' after the match – an area where journalists line up behind a barrier to interview players.

Jude Bellingham has won praise for his 'respectful' and 'classy' treatment of a female reporter.

Recent findings suggest that BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_.

'It is utter carnage,' she told BBC Radio WM, opening up on the incident at the Bernabeu. 'Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.

'Jude very rarely gives interviews, especially in the mixed zone. It is chaos... It's kind of every person out for themselves.

'You've got elbows, you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.

'I'm one of very, very few female reporters and one of very, very few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.'.

Conway admitted the mixed zone can be an 'intimidating' environment and being interrupted is unfortunately a routine part of being a post-match interviewer.

Admitting it was 'so nice' that Bellingham stepped in to stand up for her, she added: 'It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.'.

Conway, originally from Solihull, specialises in Spanish football and is based in Madrid, according to her Instagram, where she has more than 12,000 followers.

She had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort at the Bernabeu.

'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham mentioned. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

According to recent reports, 'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it. It was a nice goal and crucial for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'.

The England superstar (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

After being interrupted and encouraged by Bellingham to pose her second question, Conway asked whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country.

'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,' Bellingham added.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'.

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a latest Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Bellingham has previously earned plaudits for his treatment of the media, having stopped to speak to a disabled reporter during the World Cup when several of his England team-mates had walked past, taking the time to answer his questions in Spanish.

Breaking: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2.
  • In a recent development, common diseases are driven by a multitude of factors and remain difficult to treat given the lack of a unified disease mechanism4.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956-mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

In a recent development, common diseases are driven by a multitude of factors and remain difficult to treat given the lack of a unified disease mechanism4. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is among the most prevalent common chronic diseases, and numerous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have now identified hundreds of variants linked to CAD risk. Although these results may potentially pave the way for latest therapeutic target discovery1,2,5,6, much of the translation from GWAS to therapeutic targets for CAD has been restricted to lipid-lowering drugs7,8. Large-scale clinical studies have demonstrated a persistent residual risk of CAD independent of lipid levels9,10, but we lack drugs that directly target disease pathways in the vessel wall due to an incomplete understanding of causal disease mechanisms. Leveraging human genetics to uncover new lipid-independent biological mechanisms and drug targets in CAD represents a tremendous unmet need and would be a principal milestone in translating population-scale GWAS findings to therapies for patients11,12.

Although population-scale GWAS offer great opportunity for target discovery, most identified variants lie within non-coding regions of the genome, making it difficult to dissect the causal cell types and molecular pathways13. The advent of single-cell sequencing technologies now allows for the profiling of human tissues in health and disease at unprecedented granularity14. Previous studies have used traditional single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) for detailed characterization of cell states in human tissue that drive disease15,16,17,18; however, these studies do not profile the non-coding genome, making it challenging to link GWAS variants to observed molecular changes. More recently, single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) with sequencing (snATAC–seq) in human coronary arteries was conducted to link CAD GWAS variants to regulatory elements19. Although this represented an important advance in the field, the lack of complementary transcriptomic profiling rendered it challenging to nominate causal genes in vascular cell types. Furthermore, isolated snATAC–seq precludes the discovery of distal gene regulation as a driver of disease20, and there are right now no studies that profile the three-dimensional (3D) chromatin architecture in human coronary arteries to enable the investigation of these distal regulatory connections.

Industry observers note that herein we performed simultaneous multi-omic profiling of the transcriptome and epigenome in nuclei from 44 human coronary arteries to build a multi-omic enhancer–gene map of CAD. Collectively, these analyses identified CAD-associated regulatory variants and enhancer–gene links in smooth muscle cells (SMCs), motivating focused analysis of SMC state-dependent gene regulation. To expand insight into gene regulation across functionally heterogeneous SMC cell states, we used dynamic chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTL) modelling to uncover cell-state-dependent pathogenicity of disease variants. To dissect the role of disease-associated variants in regulating larger scale gene networks, we performed genome-wide Hi-C in 15 human coronary arteries to link variants to distal genes and validated our findings using cell-specific high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) with chromatin immunoprecipitation (Hi-ChIP–seq) and in vitro CRISPRi. Finally, we performed Perturb–seq in human coronary artery SMCs (HCASMCs) to characterize functional mechanisms of repressing disease-associated enhancers and genes. Collectively, we provide a multi-omic map of human CAD by integrating transcriptomic, epigenetic and chromatin architecture to link disease-associated genetic variants with candidate disease-relevant cell types and target genes.

We performed single-nucleus Multi-ome (RNA+ATAC) sequencing in 44 human coronary arteries from non-failing donors and patients with chronic heart failure isolated at the time of heart transplantation (Fig. 1a, Supplementary Fig. 1a and Supplementary Table 1). After quality control, we recovered 126,804 nuclei from 11 distinct cell types (Fig. 1b,c and Supplementary Fig. 1b–d). Using differential expression of canonical genes, we identified clusters corresponding to all main vascular cell types, including coronary artery SMCs (MYH11, ACTA2, ITGA8), endothelial cells (VWF, LDB2, PECAM1), fibroblasts (LAMA2, DCN, FBLN1) and myeloid cells (F13A1, CD163, MRC1) (Fig. 1b, Extended Data Fig. 1a–c and Supplementary Table 2). We used MACS2 to identify areas of open chromatin (‘peaks’) from the ATAC–seq data (Fig. 1e) and identified 143,743 cell-type-specific differentially accessible peaks (Extended Data Fig. 1d,e). Generally, cell-type clustering was concordant between the RNA and ATAC data. However, gene-expression data enabled the annotation of rarer cell types that were not captured by ATAC-based clustering alone (Supplementary Fig. 1e–g). Using differentially accessible peaks across cells, we also discovered cell-type-specific enrichment of transcriptional motifs such as SpiB and PU.1 in myeloid cells, MEF2B/C/D in SMCs and CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein in adipocytes (Supplementary Fig. 1h). We linked peaks to genes using a new supervised single-cell model called single-cell enhancer-to-gene (E2G) (scE2G)21 (Fig. 1d, Extended Data Fig. 2a–g and Supplementary Tables 3–14; Methods). We found that the non-immune cells had the greatest number of shared enhancers relative to myeloid cells (Fig. 1d) and that all cell types had a similar number of E2G links (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Table 3).

Notably, we found that cardiometabolic disease variants for CAD, systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were enriched in differentially accessible marker peaks specific to SMCs and endothelial cells (Fig. 1f). As a predominantly non-vascular trait, diabetes did not demonstrate enrichment of disease-associated variants (Fig. 1f).

Industry observers note that to boost our power for single-cell caQTL (sc-caQTL) discovery, we integrated our Multi-ome ATAC–seq data with available snATAC–seq data from human coronary arteries19 to create a meta-map of 88 samples and 245,562 nuclei across four ancestry groups (Extended Data Fig. 3a–f). We then used RASQUAL to identify pseudobulk caQTLs in four principal vascular cell types (SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts) (Fig. 2a). At the 10% false discovery rate (FDR) threshold, we found 11,269 significant caQTL associations in SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells and fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 3g–i, Supplementary Fig. 2a–d and Supplementary Tables 15–26). Power, sensitivity, subsampling and runtime analyses are shown in Supplementary Figs. 2 and 3 and described in Supplementary Methods.

It has been revealed that we further characterized caQTL variants to assess their regulatory potential. Lead caQTL variants were enriched strongly near the peaks they were predicted to regulate, consistent with a cis-regulatory mechanism (Extended Data Fig. 3j). We next overlapped our pseudobulk caQTLs and GTEx bulk arterial tissue eQTLs by cell type and found several hundred shared QTL variants in SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells and fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 3i). Furthermore, we found a strong correlation in effect size between our SMC caQTLs and bulk coronary artery eQTLs from GTEx (Extended Data Fig. 3k). Finally, in SMCs we trained a convolutional neural net model (seq2PRINT22) that incorporates chromatin accessibility and ATAC footprinting to predict transcription factor binding probability at a base-pair resolution. We found that caQTL variants within accessible peaks had significantly higher predicted transcription factor binding probabilities compared with all other non-caQTL SNP sites within accessible peaks (P = 8.2 × 10−40, Wilcoxon rank sum) (Extended Data Fig. 3l).

Sources indicate that to identify disease-associated caQTLs, we overlapped sc-caQTLs for each cell type with CAD GWAS variants (defined as lead variants associated with CAD at 1% FDR1 and variants in linkage disequilibrium with these at R2 ≥ 0.8 in the European population from 1000 Genomes Project; Supplementary Table 27), which yielded numerous disease-relevant cell-type-specific caQTLs (Extended Data Fig. 3m). For example, we found that rs7182567 was an SMC-specific caQTL that was also a GWAS variant (P = 5.4 × 10−26) and a bulk GTEx eQTL for ADAMTS7 in tibial artery (Extended Data Fig. 4a). Similarly, we found that rs8017642 is an endothelial cell-specific caQTL in the NEK9 locus (Extended Data Fig. 4b), whereas rs2337154 and rs1443120 are fibroblast- and myeloid-specific caQTLs, respectively (Extended Data Fig. 4c,d).

In a recent development, next, we leveraged the paired RNA data to sub-cluster SMCs into transcriptionally distinct cell states, forming a continuum from ‘healthy’ contractile SMC states (SMC1–3) to de-differentiated ‘disease-associated’ SMC states including fibromyocytes (FMCs) and chondromyocytes (CMCs) (Extended Data Fig. 4e). Notably, we found that ADAMTS7 was expressed most highly in FMCs (Extended Data Fig. 4e), indicating a role in disease regulation. To identify functionally distinct endothelial cell states, we mapped our data to a high-resolution scRNA-seq atherosclerosis atlas23 and identified four transcriptionally distinct endothelial subsets (Extended Data Fig. 4f). Notably, NEK9 was expressed in endothelial cells enriched with endothelium-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes such as COL1A1 and FN1 (refs. 24,25) (Extended Data Fig. 4f,g). Pathway enrichment in the EMT population showed increased EMT and stress-response signals (Extended Data Fig. 4h). Next, we created a gene set score comprised of 41 endothelial cell-specific genes thought to be associated causally with CAD26 that showed maximal enrichment in intimal endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 4i). Similarly, we created a gene signature of a gene programme26 identified previously as driving CAD pathogenesis in endothelial cells (Programme 8) and found an enrichment of this programme in angiogenic and/or vasa vasorum endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 4j).

The CAD disease-associated variant rs658956 illustrates how a cell-type-specific caQTL can impart functional transcriptional changes. The variant is an SMC-specific and fibroblast-specific caQTL and regulates a putative enhancer element (chr. 1: 59169569–59170069), which is linked to the gene FGGY-DT in an SMC-specific manner by scE2G (Fig. 2c,d). Consistently, we found that rs658956 is also a coronary artery eQTL for FGGY-DT expression (P = 3.4 × 10−12) wherein the alternative allele (T) is associated with decreased expression relative to the reference allele (G) (Fig. 2e) and is also predicted to overlie a high probability transcription factor binding site (Fig. 2f). Motif-based transcription factor binding site analysis found that rs658956 is predicted to disrupt a core AP-1 (JUN/FOS) transcription factor binding motif (5′-TGAGTCA-3′) (Fig. 2g). Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) demonstrated a binding shift in the reference allele sequence (containing G) that was not present in the alternative allele sequence (containing T) when these alleles were exposed to nuclear lysate from SMCs (Fig. 2h). Antibody supershift EMSA confirmed that the shifted AP-1 complex band consists of JUN and FOS transcription factors (Extended Data Fig. 4k). Together, these results suggest that the disease-associated variant rs658956 impacts transcription factor binding, thereby decreasing the chromatin accessibility of the enhancer and subsequently reducing FGGY-DT expression in a SMC-specific manner.

It has been revealed that in atherosclerosis, SMCs undergo a well-characterized phenotypic switch from a contractile state to a fibroblast-like FMC phenotype16, driven by disease-associated transcriptional programmes. To characterize this transition, individual nuclei were assigned an FMC score based on FMC state marker genes for downstream modelling (Fig. 2i and Extended Data Fig. 5a–d). Notably, this FMC gene score is dynamic with disease across species, disease burden, pseudotime trajectory, in vitro HCASMC stress and transcriptional regulation (Extended Data Fig. 5e–k). To identify state-dependent caQTL effects, we used a Poisson mixed-effects (PME) single-cell model (Extended Data Fig. 6a–c; Methods). Applying this PME model to the lead variants of SMC-specific pseudobulk caQTLs, we identified 712 caQTLs whose effects were dynamic with respect to the FMC score (FDR ≤ 5%) (Supplementary Tables 29 and 30). Notably, eight of these dynamic caQTLs were also disease-associated variants. For example, rs658956 exhibited a significant interaction with FMC score (FDR-adjusted likelihood ratio test (LRT) P value = 2.36 × 10−4) (Fig. 2j,k). A negative interaction term indicates that, as the FMC score increased, the negative association between rs658956 and local chromatin accessibility was amplified (Fig. 2j,k). Using the scE2G map to link dynamic caQTL-related enhancer elements (caPeaks) to target genes, we found that extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling was the most enriched pathway among linked genes (Extended Data Fig. 6d,e and Supplementary Table 31). Notably, several of these genes linked to dynamic caPeaks were enriched in FMCs (Extended Data Fig. 6f and Supplementary Table 32). Similar state-dependent effects were observed at other CAD loci such as dynamic caQTL variant rs11838776 in the COL4A1 locus, suggesting that COL4A1 may play a role during transition toward an FMC state (Extended Data Fig. 6g–k). Collectively, these dynamic analyses demonstrate that disease-associated variants can exert cell-state-dependent regulatory effects on chromatin accessibility.

To map CAD disease-associated variants to cell types and genes in an unbiased fashion, we built a disease-relevant single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map (scV2E2G) integrating cell-type-specific regulatory elements, CAD GWAS variants, scE2G links and caQTLs21,27 (Fig. 3a; Methods).

Overlapping scE2G with sc-caQTLs provides a high-fidelity set of predicted variants that may be driving disease by directly regulating intermediate molecular traits in a cell-type-specific manner.

Focusing on the 325 genes linked to SMC enhancers harbouring CAD GWAS variants, we performed several enrichment analyses. These analyses found that these linked genes were over-represented in nearest lead genes from CAD and myocardial infarction GWAS, identified GATA2 as the most enriched transcription factor and highlighted collagen and ECM remodelling as key biological processes (Extended Data Fig. 7a and Supplementary Tables 37–39). Correlation analysis between gene expression and FMC score identified FN1, COL4A1, COL4A2, MFGE8 and MYO9B—all known CAD-associated genes implicated in ECM remodelling—among the most highly correlated transcripts (Extended Data Fig. 7b and Supplementary Table 40). Notably, the enhancer harbouring variant rs7246865 emerged as potentially vital in disease, acting as both a cell-state dynamic caPeak and pseudobulk caPeak in SMCs with a high-confidence scE2G link (Fig. 3b). We confirmed this predicted link experimentally using CRISPRi in HCASMCs. Repressing the rs7246865-containing enhancer significantly reduced MYO9B expression relative to a non-targeting control (Fig. 3c), consistent with previous functional validation at this locus1. Furthermore, CRISPRi validated scE2G predictions in SMCs for three additional loci near genes LOXL1, NAV1 and PALLD; enhancer repression altered gene expression significantly at each of these loci relative to non-targeting controls (Extended Data Fig. 7c–e).

It has been revealed that to further validate scE2G links, we performed arrayed CRISPRi Perturb–seq in HCASMCs, delivering individual sgRNAs to target either the transcription start site (TSS) or the nominated enhancer at eight CAD GWAS loci (Fig. 3d, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 41). Alongside transcriptional profiling, we measured SMC proliferation by live-cell imaging, revealing that several perturbations (including ADAMTS7, CFDP1 and COL4A1) and significantly reduced proliferation rate, with enhancer knockdowns generally phenocopying their cognate TSS perturbations (Fig. 3e, Extended Data Fig. 8a and Supplementary Table 42). Following quality control, we retained 76,179 cells and confirmed robust, perturbation-specific transcriptional responses, with selective target-gene knockdown, stronger effects for TSS than enhancer perturbations and separation from non-targeting controls (Extended Data Fig. 8b–j).

Sources indicate that gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed locus-specific pathway enrichments: BMP1 and ADAMTS7 knockdowns strongly enriched MYC and E2F target-gene sets, whereas CFDP1 and COL4A1 knockdowns suppressed interferon response pathways, indicating distinct downstream transcriptional consequences across CAD loci (Extended Data Fig. 9a). Consensus non-negative matrix factorization identified six biologically interpretable programmes: inflammation, ECM remodelling, vascular remodelling, interferon response and two proliferative programmes corresponding to S and M phase (Extended Data Fig. 9b,c and Supplementary Tables 43 and 44). Notably, the ECM remodelling programme indicated the strongest positive correlation with the FMC module score, with enhancer knockdowns of CFDP1, MYO9B and BMP1 exhibiting the highest mean FMC scores (Extended Data Fig. 9d–h). Programme-level analysis further revealed that COL4A1 and its enhancer were the strongest drivers of the inflammation programme, whereas the MRAS and CFDP1 enhancer perturbations modulated both inflammation and ECM remodelling (Fig. 3f).

In a recent development, finally, robust rank aggregation (RRA) across pseudobulk DESeq2 profiles revealed a convergent gene programme dominated by downregulation of several collagen genes (COL3A1, COL4A1, COL5A1, COL6A1–A3) and TIMP2, alongside the upregulation of metabolic and stress-response genes (Fig. 3g, Extended Data Fig. 9i and Supplementary Table 45). Pathway enrichment of this convergent programme identified EMT, tumour necrosis factor signalling through nuclear factor κB, and mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 signalling as the top enriched terms (Fig. 3h). Collectively, these findings implicate a shared regulatory framework that governs SMC phenotypic states across independent, disease-associated loci.

To investigate how disease-associated variants may influence broader gene networks through chromatin looping, we performed genome-wide Hi-C in 15 human coronary arteries to construct large-scale chromatin networks (Fig. 4a, Extended Data Fig. 10a–f and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). To further complement Hi-C in bulk tissue, we performed H3K27Ac Hi-ChIP–seq in cultured human coronary artery smooth muscle cells and endothelial cells. Comparing the number of enhancer–gene connection overlap by method, we found that scE2GMulti-ome and Hi-ChIP yielded the highest number of enhancer–gene connections, with a smaller fraction from bulk coronary tissue Hi-C (Supplementary Fig. 7). We then identified groups of genomic loci that interact preferentially with one another in specific chromatin networks termed ‘mosaics’ (Fig. 4a; Methods). We identified 5,130 mosaics containing 11,494 protein-coding genes. Notably, mosaics harbouring a disease-associated variant exhibited significantly higher structural complexity, containing an average of 25 loops compared with 14 loops in non-disease-associated mosaics (P = 1.7 × 10−17) (Fig. 4b). This approach provides a framework for mapping disease-associated variants to a catalogue of genes regulated distally through interconnected chromatin networks (Supplementary Tables 46–49).
