Valencia will aim to post a third straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign at home to Osasuna on Sunday afternoon.

Los Che comfortably lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 46 wins to Osasuna's 21, while 25 of their 92 matches have finished all square.

Valencia boast a record of three wins, three draws and seven defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

It has been a tricky first third of the league season for Valencia, but there have been signs of life in recent weeks, having won two of their last three in the league and three of their last four in all competitions.

Javier Aguirre's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano in La Liga, while they also beat Tavernes 6-0 in the Copa del Rey on November 10.

Valencia, who finished ninth in Spain's top flight last season, actually have the second-worst home record in La Liga this season, securing only two points from seven league games in front of their own supporters.

Los Che are also the joint-second lowest goalscorers in La Liga this term with nine, and that is a concerning record heading towards the winter break in Spain's top flight.

As for Osasuna, a record of four wins, three draws and six defeats from 13 matches has brought them 15 points, which is enough for 13th spot at this stage of proceedings.

Jagoba Arrasate's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Malaga, but they did lose their last away fixture - a 2-1 reverse to Deportivo La Coruna on November 2.

Los Rojillos have struggled on their travels this season, claiming only three points from six matches, suffering five defeats in the process.

Osasuna lost 1-0 to Valencia in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign, and they have only managed to win one of the last five games between the two sides.

That said, Osasuna do have a recent away success against Valencia to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory at Mestalla in August 2023.

Osasuna form (all competitions):.

Valencia will welcome Jose Gaya back into their squad this weekend following a suspension, but Sergi Canos, Diego Lopez and Jesus Vazquez are again expected to miss the contest.

Arnaut Danjuma is likely to return to the squad, with the attacker not involved against Rayo Vallecano last time out following the death of his father.

Gaya for Pablo Maffeo could be the only change from the team's last match given the impressive nature of both the performance and the result.

As for Osasuna, Alejandro Catena is out of the game through suspension, with the 32-year-old sent off in the team's home success over Malaga last time out.

Jorge Herrando was back on the bench against Malaga after recovering from an injury and could now be introduced into the starting team here.

Ante Budimir has scored nine times in 13 league appearances this season, and the Croatian will once again lead the Osasuna line in this contest.

However, Abel Bretones, Aitor Fernandez and Rockson Yeboah are still injured.

Herrera; Rosier, Herrando, Boyomo, Rico; Moncayola, Gomez; Ruben Garcia, Oroz, Barja; Budimir.

A stalemate could be on the cards at Mestalla.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.

In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.

Sources indicate that still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," noted Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement. Denmark is leading the way across all four categories assessed — energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and national climate policy. A total of 15 states, including Lithuania, Chile, and Morocco, received an overall "high" rating, which is two more than last year.

The European Union also moved up a spot, while Hungary jumped 21 places after the ousting of former prime minister Viktor Orban's government, which had repeatedly vetoed EU climate plans, dismissing them as a "utopian fantasy.".

The top three positions on the CCPI remained vacant again this year, as no country has yet done enough to meet global climate goals aimed at preventing worsening weather extremes and climate damage.

In a recent development, "We are seeing a striking contrast," mentioned Burck. "Progress on climate action is often slow and in some countries, such as the United States, things are even moving backwards. But technologically and economically there is enormous momentum.".

That momentum is apparent in record solar energy growth. Last year 75% of global electricity demand growth was met by the green energy source, according to energy think tank Ember's latest global electricity review. Investment in clean energy has also outpaced that in fossil fuels for multiple years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rapid expansion of renewable technology, as well as the Iran War and a reduction in deforestation are behind a projected slight fall in emissions for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the CCPI.

"Governments have to act now to turn the momentum into sustained emissions reductions," stated CCPI co-author Niklas Höhne of the NewClimate Institute, which compiles the report with environmental NGO Germanwatch.

Burck attributed Germany's worst ever performance in the category of national climate policy to current policies being pursued by Germany's economy minister Katherina Reiche.

"Measures that primarily aim to increase the use of natural gas, threaten to undermine progress in the energy transition and risk significantly worsening the conditions for renewable energy and electrification for many years to come," mentioned Burck.

A European Commission report published on November 9 on the sidelines of the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey mentioned Germany was one of nine EU countries set to miss 2030 emissions reductions targets.

In a recent development, germany is not alone in its disappointing ranking. The other G20 countries — the world's leading industrialized and emerging economies, responsible for around 80% of global CO2 emissions — also perform poorly.

The only exception among them is the United Kingdom, which ranks seventh and received a high rating, performing well in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and climate policy. However, study authors rated it low for renewable energy expansion.

In a recent development, the G20's oil- and gas-producing countries occupy some of the lowest positions on the climate action table. The United States, which is the world's second largest emitter, languishes alongside Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Canada around the bottom of the league, with an overall rating of "very low.".

The hosts of this year's COP31, also received a "low" overall score. Australia, a major coal exporter with some of the world's highest per-capita emissions, ranks 54th, while Turkey, which is also heavily dependent on fossil fuels, comes in 53rd.

China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases and ranks 56th in the CCPI, receiving an overall rating of "very low." Its main weaknesses include its now high per-capita emissions and substantial energy consumption.

However, among the G20, China leads the way in renewable energy expansion. The country, which is five years ahead of schedule in reaching its goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030, also produces over 80% of the world's solar panels.

Several oil-producing countries, including Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates, are also performing better than expected in the renewables category and "are significantly expanding their previously limited" capacity, said the report.

The authors said these countries have significant potential to further expand renewables.

"In the Arab states in particular, very high per-capita emissions and an above-average level of electrification coincide with a relatively low existing share of renewable energy and enormous solar potential," stated co-author Natalie Pelekh in a statement. "These are, in fact, ideal conditions for more ambitious climate action.".

This article was originally published in German.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:48 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 10:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

A referee was replaced at half-time of an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match after he was accused of 'being drunk' by a manager of one of the teams – a claim the official has denied.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab oversaw the match between United Arab Emirates' side Al Jazira and Iran's Gol Gohar in Asia's second tier club competition.

Controversy emerged in the 32nd minute after Hattab awarded a free-kick after a foul by Al Jazira's Felício Milson.

Hattab initially waved away protests from Al-Jazira players and approached Milson holding a yellow card.

The official then stunned players after appearing to receive a message in his earpiece, before turning and walking towards Al-Jazira goalkeeper Ersin Destanoglu.

Hattab showed the goalkeeper a yellow card, despite him being nearly half the pitch away from the incident.

Referee Hanna Hattab was accused by a manager of 'being drunk' following a controversial decision in an Asian Champions League Two match - a claim the official has denied.

The referee was then seen speaking to his fourth official, leading to him rescinding the goalkeeper's yellow card while Milson escaped being shown a second yellow card for his challenge.

Al Jazira scored the only goal of the game minutes later through Anderson Talisca, but the bizarre incident involving Hattab was reportedly the centre of discussion at half-time.

Gol Gohar head coach Mehdi Rahmati had reportedly been seen shouting 'he's drunk' at the official, while the club's sporting director claimed post-match they would have refused to play the second half had Hattab remained in charge.

'The referee against Al Jazira was not in a normal state, and even Al Jazira's players told us the same thing,' said Heydar Afsari.

'The club immediately informed the match officials and warned them that we would not play if the situation remained the same.'.

Hattab was ultimately replaced by the fourth official for the second half of the match.

The referee, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing pool, has since released a statement hitting back at the allegation.

'I will wait for the official communication and official stance from the Syrian Arab Football Federation, and I will also communicate with the people and parties responsible for me locally and internationally, before issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened,' Hattab wrote.

The claim had centred on the referee appearing to listen to his earpiece and changing his mind on booking an Al Jazira player, before bizarrely showing a yellow card to their goalkeeper.

Al Jazira's goalkeeper appeared stunned by his yellow card, which was later rescinded with the referee then being replaced at half-time of the match.

'In conclusion, I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands.

'Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them.

'I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.'.

Omani sports journalist Issa Mentioned, who covers Asian competitions, also came to Hattab's defence and insisted the claim the official was drunk is false.

'What happened to him was due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus,' he wrote on social media,.

'He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating.'.

The Syrian Football Federation added in a statement: 'Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media- that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded.

'The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident.

'In this regard, the Committee has contacted the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to request the referee’s medical report, the match commissioner’s report, and the referee assessor’s report, in order to accurately ascertain the facts of the incident and take the necessary follow-up actions.'.

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 10:13, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:16.

Two teams enjoying solid campaigns in Spain's top flight thus far will lock horns on Sunday evening, as Real Sociedad welcome Sevilla to Anoeta Stadium.

Real Sociedad just about lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 55 victories to Sevilla's 52, while 35 of their 142 fixtures have finished level.

Real Sociedad will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Europa League, with the result leaving them down in 27th spot in the overall table and out of the knockout round playoffs at this stage of proceedings.

It has been a struggle for Real Sociedad in Europe this season, and they were also beaten 3-2 by Racing de Santander in Spain's top flight last weekend, so the Basque team will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions on Sunday night.

La Real have had a strong campaign in Spain's top flight, with a record of seven wins, one draw and five defeats from 13 matches bringing them 22 points, which is enough for fifth spot in the La Liga table.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side now have three straight league games against Sevilla, Real Madrid and Villarreal before returning to European action at home to Torreense on December 10.

Real Sociedad have been strong at home in the league this season, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat, picking up 13 points from six matches.

Sevilla have won five, drawn four and lost four of their 13 league matches this season, with 19 points leaving them in sixth spot in the table, three points behind fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

The Red and Whites are without a win in their last three La Liga fixtures, though, losing at Getafe at the start of the month before drawing back-to-back games with Alaves and Real Betis.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only actually won one of their last seven league matches, but sitting sixth after 13 games represents a solid start to the campaign.

Sevilla recorded a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad when the two teams last locked horns in May 2026, but the corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 success for the Basque outfit.

Los Nervionenses have picked up eight points from their six away league matches during the 2026-27 campaign courtesy of a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Real Sociedad at the moment have a number of injury complications, with Yangel Herrera, Alvaro Odriozola, Ander Barrenetxea, Jon Aramburu and Lander Astiazaran on the sidelines.

Head coach Matarazzo will make changes to the side that started against Palace in the Europa League, with Carlos Soler, Orri Oskarsson, Igor Zubeldia, Sergio Gomez and Luka Sucic among those set to return to the team for this match.

Mikel Oyarzabal has only scored three times this season, but the Spain international will continue in the final third of the field for the Basque outfit.

Sevilla will once again be without the services of Marcao, Jose Angel Carmona, Alfon Gonzalez and Miguel Sierra on Sunday due to injury problems.

However, the visitors did not suffer any fresh challenges against Real Betis last time out, and given the strength of the performance, it could be a case of same again in terms of team selection.

Isaac Romero and Robbie Ure are both pushing to be included in the final third of the field, but the expectation is that Lucas Stassin will again be given the nod in that area.

Remiro; Fort, Zubeldia, Sarr, Gomez; Sucic, Gorrotxategi, Soler, Guedes; Oyarzabal, Oskarsson.

Sevilla possible starting lineup:.

Vlachodimos; Iglesias Sanchez, Castrin, Salas, Suazo; Agoume, Guridi; Vargas, Fofana, Correia; Stassin.

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

Sources indicate that “You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

Industry observers note that this was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and noted “stop”.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

In a recent development, arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

#152110. DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's notable.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (930 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's notable.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black?
  • Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?
  • Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes.

Your brain has its own version of that.

Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?

Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.

It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas.

That's your brain's default mode network.

Scientists conducted brain-imaging experiments in the 1990s and early 2000s to find out which regions of the brain were active during demanding tasks, like solving a math problem or memory exercise.

Sources indicate that but to measure that, they needed a so-called baseline. They needed to know the level of brain activity at rest and during demanding tasks.

So, between the tasks, they asked participants to relax, close their eyes, stare at a fixed point on a wall, or try not to think of anything at all.

And they measured the participants' brain activity both when they were solving a task and doing nothing. That's how scientists noticed the brain was active in up- and downtime.

It has been revealed that they noticed that when participants started to focus on a new task, after having done nothing, some brain areas lit up and other areas dimmed down. That suggests those areas that dimmed down must have been active while the participant was apparently — physically and mentally — at rest.

This realization eventually led to the discovery of the default mode network or DMN.

The DMN is crucial because it helps your brain make sense of your life and experiences.

It helps you connect and revisit memories, reflect on who you are, imagine what might happen in future scenarios, understand other people, build meaning from experience, and connect ideas in latest ways.

Industry observers note that it turns all your memories, experiences, knowledge, emotions and social information into your internal story. Think of that story as a constantly evolving, updated model of who you are and how you engage with the world around you.

But it's key to understand the DMN involves more than one area of the brain. It is a group of brain regions that light up when you're not focused on an external task.

There's another player in your brain that acts as a monitoring system. You can think of it as constantly asking "Is there anything that needs my attention?".

Imagine you're daydreaming while driving, and a car suddenly swerves into your lane.

In a fraction of a second, your daydream disappears and your attention snaps back to the road. That player is called the salience network, or SN.

The salience network helps you notice crucial signals, like a sound, a mistake, pain, an emotion, a threat, or something happening in your body, and helps shift the brain toward attention and control systems when action is needed.

The DMN, SN and attention/control systems constantly interact.

And the DMN doesn't just turn off completely with every hard task. Parts of it can also contribute when tasks involve memory, stories, meaning or other people.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Smartphones have filled many of the small empty moments of our days — waiting for the bus, standing in line, eating alone, lying on the couch. We are constantly looking at our devices.

So, it seems reasonable to ask: are we crowding out those moments of boredom where DMN kicks in?

It has been revealed that maybe. But so far, there's no strong evidence that scrolling directly affects mental health by reducing DMN time.

What we do know is that problematic smartphone use can increase stress, anxiety, task-switching and disrupt sleep.

And sleep loss and stress also have clearer evidence for altering DMN-related brain connectivity.

The DMN is not always necessarily good.

When your mind wanders, it might produce a great new idea.

But it might also replay an embarrassing thing you did five years ago. Again. And again.

In depression, the self-reflection part of the DMN can get caught in repetitive negative loops that are hard to stop — what's known as rumination.

Sources indicate that scientists have also found that Alzheimer's disease targets key DMN areas, particularly those responsible for your autobiographical memory and remembering other aspects of the past. Which may help explain why memory problems are so central to the disease.

Protect your sleep and take stress seriously. There is direct evidence that sleep loss and stress disrupt DMN-related connectivity.

Take real, quiet breaks after mentally demanding tasks, like studying. It can even help you memorize facts for your exam.

Embrace boredom and enjoy doing nothing.

Try to reframe boredom as this essential, energy-intensive active work in your brain that builds your internal narrative and sense of self, consolidates memories, creates connections and sparks creativity.

Recent findings suggest that try waiting in line without checking your phone. Look out the window next time you take the bus or take a walk without listening to anything.

You can also try scheduling DMN time. It may be the closest thing to a real brain hack.

Liverpool are full of confidence as they travel to face rivals Everton in the latest Merseyside derby on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola’s surging Reds have been piling up the goals since the November international break - scoring seven times across their last two fixtures alone.

A hugely satisfying 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United at Anfield last weekend in what was Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge of the visitors was swiftly followed by a 3-0 victory in the Champions League away at Club Brugge.

Unbeaten in five Premier League matches, Fulham welcome in-form Bournemouth to Craven Cottage for Sunday's matchweek 12 encounter.

While Alvaro Arbeloa's team have struggled for goals during their unbeaten run, the Cherries recorded a 10th consecutive victory on Thursday, with five of those wins coming in the top flight.

After a slow start to life under Arbeloa, Fulham have gradually found their feet under the former Real Madrid boss.

The Cottagers began the 2026-27 season by collecting just two points from a possible 18, although their four opening defeats were all narrow, but the capital club have since turned their form around.

Fulham have collected nine points from an available 15, making the West Londoners one of the division's form sides ahead of this weekend's fixtures.

However, the 15th-placed side remain hampered by two challenges: their attacking inefficiency and inability to protect leads, highlighted by Arbeloa's men scoring exactly once in seven consecutive matches and dropping 10 points from winning positions.

Only Brentford (11) have surrendered more points after taking the lead, and addressing both weaknesses could determine whether the improving Cottagers remain in the bottom half or challenge for a top-half finish or European qualification.

Bournemouth, though, have no such concerns heading into Sunday, with Marco Rose's men flying high domestically and in Europe.

Thursday's victory over Celta Vigo preserved their perfect record atop the Europa League standings after five rounds of the eight-match league phase, while their domestic turnaround since a 5-1 hammering at Stamford Bridge has been striking.

After failing to keep a clean sheet in their opening six league matches under the latest manager, the Cherries have shut out four of their next five opponents, with a maximum return of 15 points propelling them to fifth in the Premier League table.

While Bournemouth cannot overtake fourth-placed Liverpool this matchweek, they could strengthen their grip on fifth if the teams below them stumble.

Having watched their side win five of the last eight top-flight meetings with Fulham, the travelling supporters will hope for another positive result against the London club to secure a sixth consecutive league victory and an 11th across all competitions.

The hosts' improvement under their Spanish boss, however, suggests that the Dorset-based visitors will encounter stern resistance at Craven Cottage, adding to the intrigue surrounding this weekend's contest.

Joshua King is the only Fulham player to have scored more than once, with his two goals complemented by strikes from Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Cesar Palacios, Gonzalo Garcia, Oscar Bobb and Ryan Sessegnon.

Bournemouth, meanwhile, owe much of their league position to Evanilson and Marcus Tavernier, whose combined 11 goals account for 61% of their 18 top-flight strikes in 2026-27.

Like Fulham, the visitors have most of their squad available, although Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) and Alex Toth (thigh) are absent; Julian Araujo faces a late assessment as he targets a return from a thigh problem, while Junior Kroupi will be checked after falling ill before Thursday's comeback victory over Celta.

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally expected to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a pre-agreement contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their aims after he impressed during Chelsea trials.

Zongo made his senior international debut for Burkina Faso aged just 16 last month, when he came off the bench to play in the second half of a 7-0 friendly defeat by Argentina in Buenos Aires.

It has been revealed that the teenager previously impressed when he starred for Burkina Faso on their run to the quarter-finals of the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar last autumn. The midfielder scored the winner as his nation stunned Germany in the round of 16.

Scouts from a number of top European clubs were in attendance at games across the tournament and many took note of the performances produced by Zongo, who was 15 at the time.

Zongo had previously been linked with several other suitors, including LaLiga outfit Villarreal.

#152103. Tech Report: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

Tech Report: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a upcoming flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andoni Iraola insisted Liverpool's recent turnaround in form was "not about Florian Wirtz or Alexander Isak".

The Reds have won each of their last three games in all competitions, following up a 4-0 win over Manchester United in the Premier League with a 3-0 Champions League victory at Club Brugge.

Isak scored twice in the win against Brugge, while also netting in their league victory over Crystal Palace before the international break.

Wirtz also found the back of the net in midweek in the Champions League, while he has both scored and assisted a goal in his last two Premier League appearances.

The only Liverpool player to do so three times in a row is Mohamed Salah, who did it twice, in December 2018 and October 2021.

However, Iraola believes his whole Liverpool team have made improvements on the ball in recent weeks.

"For me, it is not about Florian or Alex," mentioned Iraola.

It has been revealed that "If we play well, someone will score a goal, give an assist, make the numbers. It's about how those players help us play well.

"If we have a good offensive volume, someone will score the goals. We have been good in possession in the last few games, I think we are improving a lot on the ball.".

“It’s a massive game for everyone involved and I’m very happy to be part of it.”  https://t.co/rYdhYlcTv7.

— Liverpool FC (@LFC) November 27, 2026.

Liverpool face Everton this weekend in Iraola's first Merseyside derby since taking over from Arne Slot.

Liverpool have lost just one of their last 15 Premier League away games against Everton (W4 D10), with 10 of their last 14 visits finishing level.

"I haven't lived this derby," stated the Spaniard. "But it doesn't take a lot when you are here to decide it's a massive game for everybody involved.

Industry observers note that "I am very happy to be part of it and I really hope I enjoy it. To enjoy it, there is only one way, to win the game.

Industry observers note that "Derbies are always different. It doesn't matter where you are in the standings. Normally, the type of game is different and you can feel it from the beginning.

"We have to do our part, our duels, be at a good level. We have to know it's a derby and also be good on the ball, quality wise.".

Latest Update: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1327 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.
  • "The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.
  • A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by New Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres said the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach.".

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, stated that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he noted, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "latest era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including major polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

According to recent reports, financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

Recent findings suggest that erdogan said while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest.".

"Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she mentioned, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

Industry observers note that most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, mentioned the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and swiftly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over.".

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," said Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

"We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine noted.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Albanese mentioned it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most.".

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she mentioned, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres said, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

Sources indicate that von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands stated electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian stated his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms.".

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he said.

Recent findings suggest that he also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he said.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Latest transfer news and rumours.

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year, writes Dom Smith.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally due to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, stated that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their prepares after he impressed during trials.

Click here to read the full story.

Manchester United have reportedly activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.

The influential Red Devils captain was previously set to see his deal at Old Trafford expire in the summer, with speculation that he could depart after previous strong links to Saudi Arabia.

But United always possessed the option to trigger an automatic one-year extension, which they have now done.

Fernandes’ contract is now valid until June 2028, but The Athletic’s David Ornstein reports that such an extension will not necessarily prevent the Portugal playmaker from leaving next summer.

It means that if he does go, then United will at least receive a transfer fee.

Manchester United have a potential ace up their sleeve in transfer talks over Nico Paz.

Argentine star Paz is enjoying a burgeoning reputation across Europe after a remarkable start to the season with Como, which has seen him score six goals from attacking midfield - including two against Man Utd in the Champions League last month.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not at the moment favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is said to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of latest manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

Industry observers note that “That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic noted in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they said they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

It has been revealed that “Tottenham mentioned they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”.

The German defender previously spent five years at Stamford Bridge before leaving for Real Madrid in 2022.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea could make a cut-price swoop to bring Rudiger back to west London before his current contract at the Bernabeu expires next summer.

He is struggling for game time under Jose Mourinho, while Xabi Alonso needs to rapidly improve a defence that is leaking goals.

It looks like Arsenal will face a major fight from Manchester United over Nico Paz.

As mentioned already this morning, the Gunners are believed to be closely monitoring Como’s rising superstar, along with the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham.

But The Athletic’s David Ornstein now claims that Manchester United will pursue Paz if captain Bruno Fernandes leaves the club this summer, with a switch to Old Trafford said to hold some appeal for the Argentine.

It looks like Paz does not want to return to Real Madrid as things stand currently, despite their €80m buy-back clause.

Manchester United look to have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Maxi Araujo.

The Uruguay and Sporting defender has emerged as a potential candidate to become Mauricio Pochettino’s first Old Trafford signing during the January transfer window as the latest manager seeks to improve his options at left-back.

According to Sport Witness, Araujo’s camp are open to the move, which could apparently cost around €50m-€60m despite the €80m release clause in his contract at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Arsenal are interested in a blockbuster deal for Nico Paz, reports claim.

The Argentine playmaker has been central to the stunning rise of Serie A side Como under ex-Gunners star Cesc Fabregas, having left Real Madrid for Italy in 2024.

Los Blancos have a buy-back option for Paz next summer stated to be valued at around €80m, though he is also attracting plenty of interest from elsewhere.

CaughtOffside cite reports claiming that Arsenal are closely tracking the 22-year-old, along with Liverpool and Tottenham, with a return to Madrid looking unlikely as things stand.

Richarlison is open to moving to Saudi Arabia to end his Tottenham exile.

The striker has been frozen out at Spurs by manager Roberto De Zerbi after failing to agree a summer exit.

Everton, Vasco da Gama and Trabzonspor were all stated to have explored deals for Richarlison, who ended up staying put at Spurs despite being left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad.

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 10:50.
  • Two Serie A strugglers will meet in this week's Sunday lunchtime kickoff, as Udinese and Fiorentina vie for three precious points.
  • That tally separates the sides after 12 matchdays, with the hosts trailing behind their Viola visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 10:50.

Two Serie A strugglers will meet in this week's Sunday lunchtime kickoff, as Udinese and Fiorentina vie for three precious points.

That tally separates the sides after 12 matchdays, with the hosts trailing behind their Viola visitors.

Having sacked Kosta Runjaic after an awful run of seven defeats from eight games, Udinese are still waiting to see an upturn since Paolo Zanetti took charge.

Zanetti started with a loss to relegation rivals Venezia before the international break, then saw his side fight scrap out a 1-1 draw with Bologna when they returned to action last week.

Against one of Serie A's form teams, that was a good result in isolation, but the Friulani still have just one league win so far - against newly promoted Monza, way back at the end of August.

Since then, their season has unravelled completely, and picking up two points from 10 matches has left them stuck inside the drop zone.

Now heading back to Udine, the Bianconeri have already equalled their worst home record at this stage of a top-flight campaign, and they are right now on a run of five straight defeats at Bluenergy Stadium.

Perhaps the only positive omens are that they comfortably won this equivalent fixture last season, and that Fiorentina are also in freefall.

It was a tale of two massive home wins when the pair met last term, with the Friuli club responding to a 5-1 loss in Florence by winning 3-0 a few weeks later.

This time, Fiorentina will head north in a similar state of distress to Udinese, having lost once again on Monday night.

Failing to build on a promising draw against Juventus, the Viola sunk to a 3-0 defeat in Monza, leaving them 16th in the Serie A table and just one point above the drop zone.

Making their worst start since 2001, they have now lost seven of their first 12 fixtures and are yet to keep a clean sheet.

In fact, Fiorentina have conceded at least twice in all of the last seven, as Paolo Vanoli struggles to pull off the same salvage job he managed last term.

Vanoli was rehired earlier this season, but after recently sandwiching an away win over Sassuolo with a pair of home draws, Monday's meltdown has sent Fiorentina fans even deeper into despair.

Udinese boss Zanetti is still missing Nicolo Bertola, who recently joined Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines, while last season's top scorer Keinan Davis is a doubt.

The latter has been struggling with an adductor problem, and the Friulani's forwards have only contributed three league goals so far.

According to recent reports, at least Nicolo Zaniolo seems to be finding some form, with two in his last three appearances - as many as across the previous 28. Zaniolo once spent a fruitless loan spell at Fiorentina, but he has previously scored twice against the Viola in Serie A.

There were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

Industry observers note that the first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

According to recent reports, olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

The trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

According to recent reports, as if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

With just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays demonstrated it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

Sources indicate that the finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.
  • Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 26 November 2026.

Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).

The young United centre-back was shown a straight red card after VAR doubled down on the day, insisting that no ‘clear and obvious error’ had been made.

United successfully appealed the decision through an independent panel and the lengths they went to for their evidence submission has now come to light.

Bosses at United included three high-definition video clips of the incident in question, which used multiple different angles as well as speeds in slow-motion and in real time for the panel to consider.

United also submitted video evidence of a DOGSO sending off earlier this season for Brighton’s Pascal Struijk against Sunderland, which was also overturned on appeal.

Leny Yoro was sent off for Man United against Liverpool but the red card was later rescinded.

United demonstrated that Isak would not have reached the ball if he'd have stayed on his feet.

The most fascinating element of United’s detailed evidence pack came via its data department, led by ex-Formula One guru Michael Sansoni.

United outlined in a letter to the appeal panel that a technical analysis of the incident saw boffins at Carrington calculate the probability of Isak reaching the ball following his heavy touch prior to contact from Yoro.

The data allowed for the possibility that Isak maintained his speed and direction from the moment his legs first made contact with Yoro to assess whether he would have got to the ball before United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

United’s analysis concluded that Isak would have been 1.8 metres shy of reaching the ball even if all optimal speed and directional factors had been achieved.

The appeals commission, however, told United that that data, however detailed, was not verifiable and so had to be treated with ‘caution’.

Considering all the elements of United’s submission, the panel unanimously agreed that it was not a red card offence and did not meet the threshold for DOGSO, immediately overturning the decision and withdrawing all punishment against Yoro.

‘We can accept referee can make a mistake. But we have VAR. What were they doing?’ a fuming Mauricio Pochettino said on Tuesday of the original Yoro decision.

‘We are going to repeat the game? Play similar tools the game XI v XI? We have an unbelievable car but we have to be at the level to drive. We accept the technology.’.

Chelsea are allegedly yet to determine whether they will consider ending Alejandro Garnacho's loan stint at Aston Villa.

On Tuesday evening, the Argentine was left out of the squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Unai Emery naming two goalkeepers and having one spare spot on the substitutes' bench.

Emery suggested after the game that he only selected players who he felt were capable of making an impact in that particular match, essentially delivering a clear message to Garnacho.

Garnacho has been restricted to just seven substitute appearances totalling fewer than 100 minutes since making the loan switch to Villa, who can activate a permanent £43m transfer if the winger plays a set number of matches.

However, like in the case of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott in 2025-26, it has become apparent that Emery has given up on a loan player who Villa could sign for substantial money if they make in the region of eight to 10 appearances.

As per several reports, Villa do not have the option of ending Garnacho's loan during the winter transfer window, nor do Chelsea have a recall clause.

These were the same terms that Villa and Liverpool agreed for Elliott, and subsequently failed to agree over a compromise for the second half of the last campaign.

According to The Athletic, Villa will need to hope that a foreign club expresses an interest in signing Garnacho at the turn of the year.

Garnacho is said to have wanted to leave the Premier League for a European club prior to Emery expressing an interest in his services.

At this point in time, though, it is unclear whether Chelsea would give the green light to a change of clubs for Garnacho.

If it is not beneficial from a financial perspective, they may choose to take no action.

In a recent development, the exact reason why Emery wanted to sign Garnacho is unclear. The fact that the former Manchester United attacker has not made a single start is either reflective of his efforts in training or Emery not having any serious interest in a permanent deal.

Either way, it is clear that Garnacho needs to rebuild his career in Europe, most likely La Liga where he has previously spent time at Atletico Madrid as a youngster.

According to recent reports, how that may come about remains to be seen. Any club would likely have to take the bulk of Garnacho's wages and pay a substantial loan fee for it to be worthwhile to Chelsea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jarrod Bowen has admitted that talks over his West Ham future will take place if a return to the Premier League is not secured this season.

The West Ham captain, who played his 300th game for the club this week, was the subject of Premier League interest at the end of last season following the club’s relegation to the second division for the first time in 14 years, but never considered leaving.

Bowen instead committed his immediate future to West Ham by signing a latest contract, which included revised terms to help the club in their bid for promotion.

The 29-year-old claims it was an easy decision to stay, but conversations will need to be had if West Ham are resigned to a second season in the second tier.

You don't want to be stuck, you want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away.

The Hammers have endured a tricky start to life in the Championship, and currently sit outside the play-off places and winless in four games under fresh manager Scott Parker.

“I never wanted to leave after being relegated,” Bowen tells Standard Sport.

“I always wanted to give it an opportunity, to go we can get this club back into the Premier League. I wanted to be the spearhead of that.

“I think it's wrong to look too far ahead into the future because I think your energy has to be into this season. But if it doesn't happen, then we will sit down and have a conversation at the end of the season.

“But I think for now, we have to put all our energy into this season because there's something special that we can achieve.”.

West Ham have struggled to adapt to the Championship, winning six of their opening 17 games, but Bowen notes this came as no surprise to him and believes promotion expert Parker can turn things around.

“He's been brilliant,” Bowen indicates of former Hammers midfielder Parker, who has earned promotion from the Championship on three seperate occasions. “Someone who understands the club, played so many years here, captained here at this club as well. He's been a breath of fresh air since he's been here.

“We've only worked together a few weeks. Obviously, the results haven't been the way that we wanted. Some of the performances that we've had, we probably deserve more from some of the games.

“We feel we're in a weirdly good place, and we're looking forward to what we've got coming up.”.

An edgy 1-0 victory at Swansea last month felt at the time like the making of West Ham as promotion candidates, but they are yet to taste victory since Parker replaced Nuno Espirito Santo in the dugout last month.

The 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth this week prompted Parker to warn that West Ham risk getting stuck in the Championship if they do not adapt to the physical demands of the league.

And Bowen insists promotion back to the top flight is not as easy as some make out.

“Of course you don't want to be stuck,” he continued. “You want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away, of course you do.

“But like I said, it's not as easy as what people think or just to expect. Just because you've come down, it'll be easy for you to get back promoted because that's not the case, and we're finding that out right now.”.

Bowen was speaking to Standard Sport at the EFL’s Power of 72 event at the London Stadium, promoting West Ham’s Thrive employability programme, which concentrates on providing support to Neet (not in education, employment or training) and underemployed young people in Newham and east London.

EFL Power of 72 celebrates the positive impact EFL Clubs have on their communities and the bond between clubs and local people, with one million people participating in EFL club charity programmes every season.

“It's so crucial to me because it's something that I've been involved in for a few years now since I've been here,” Bowen mentioned of the Thrive employability programme.

“We have people with different backgrounds, different upbringings, that all have limited opportunities to go out and showcase that. So, the work we're doing is giving them the opportunity to go and showcase what they want to do, giving them the work experience to go on and achieve what they set out to do.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:44.

The stuttering champions and the challengers-in-crisis face off in Sunday's Premier League main event, which sees Arsenal and Manchester City draw swords at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners hold a six-point advantage over Enzo Maresca's men at the summit of the Premier League table, leading some to deduce that another success for the holders could already expel the Sky Blues from the title race.

Out of sight in first place, boasting the best defence in the top flight and taking 16 points from the last 18 on offer in the Premier League, Arsenal have lived up to their early-season expectations as the overwhelming favourites to retain their crown.

Yet, the Emirates faithful cannot shake the feeling that there is still something missing in Mikel Arteta's ranks, after Arsenal's second-half shortcomings were exposed in back-to-back draws with Newcastle United and Borussia Dortmund.

Both stalemates saw the Gunners fail to hold onto and build on one-goal advantages in the first half, before their foes came out all guns blazing after the restart and capitalised on Arsenal's alarming lack of a ruthless attacking touch.

Only four of Arsenal's 30 shots on goal in the Champions League were on target, as their 12-game winning run in home league phase/group stage fixtures came to an end, and their 17 Premier League goals scored so far ranks as the worst among all top-six teams.

However, the holders are five from five at the Emirates Stadium in the top flight - scoring 10 times and conceding just twice in the process - and they are yet to draw a blank at home in any tournament this term.

Interestingly, Arsenal's 10 home goals matches Man City's 10 away strikes in the 2026-27 Premier League season, while only Brighton & Hove Albion (26) can better the visitors' overall total of 22.

Such statistics will come as little consolation to travelling fans amid the Sky Blues' sorry slump, though, as Enzo Maresca's men have collected just one point from the last 12 on offer in the top flight after a perfect seven from seven to start the campaign.

The Citizens at least managed to snap their three-game losing sequence in last week's 1-1 draw at home to Fulham - not that such a feat was worth celebrating, though - before they also had to settle for a point in their midweek Champions League clash with Napoli.

Maresca and former Man City players have disagreed over whether the club's guilty verdict and appeal uncertainty over their 115 charges is impacting on-field performances, but the manager himself now finds himself under fire for questionable tactical calls and team selections over the autumnal period.

There is no suggestion that the former Chelsea boss is under any immediate sack pressure, though, despite presiding over a 122-year worst; City are just the second team in English Football League history to win their first seven matches of a season but fail to triumph in any of their next four, after the 1904-05 Sheffield Wednesday crop.

Furthermore, the Sky Blues were swatted aside in August's 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal, who have only lost two of their last nine head-to-heads against Man City and are unbeaten in their last three meetings on Emirates soil.

Arsenal form (all competitions):.

Manchester City Premier League form:.

Manchester City form (all competitions):.

Fears of a serious shoulder injury to Arsenal number one David Raya have been allayed by Arteta, and at the time of writing, the Spain international has not been officially ruled out of the visit of Man City.

Arsenal will also welcome teenage wonderkid Max Dowman back from a three-game domestic suspension, but Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) and Bukayo Saka (quad) will not be back until just before Christmas at the earliest.

After Christos Tzolis's underwhelming midweek display, expect Eberechi Eze to return to the forward line, where Arteta has a critical choice to make between Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz after the former's thunderous finish in midweek.

Meanwhile, captain Martin Odegaard has another Premier League record in his sights; if he sets up two goals here, he will equal the record for the most assists by a Norwegian player in the competition - his 38 is marginally inferior to Morten Gamst Pedersen's 40.

Meanwhile, Man City are expected to head south with a fully-fit squad barring former Arsenal transfer target Antoine Semenyo, who is a few weeks away from returning from a knee injury.

Snubbed from the starting XI against Fulham before saving City's skin against Napoli, Rayan Cherki has surely done enough to hold his spot at the Emirates, while Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye also have cases to come back in after providing assists off the bench last time out.

Goalless in his last three Premier League matches, Erling Haaland could equal his own personal worst for an English top-flight goal drought, having never gone longer than four Premier League games without finding the back of the net.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Nunes, Guehi, Dias, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

The defensive numbers make for dreadful reading for Man City, who have let in seven goals across their last three away games and are without a clean sheet in 10 fixtures in total.

A profligate Arsenal side may not be the best-placed to capitalise, as only one of their last five wins has been by more than a one-goal margin, but the champions should still demonstrate why they are champions and deal another blow to Man City's already-fading title hopes.

#152091. Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
